name: Voltframe Chrome-Rave Showcase Rig
description: A Tier 2 circuit-club staple built specifically to make augmented limbs the centerpiece of the look. The base is a sleeveless compression bodysuit in gunmetal grey with open-lattice panels at the shoulders, hips, and ribs — structural voids that frame chrome arm augmentations like sculpture. The fabric is reactive synthweave that picks up bass frequencies and ripples with slow amber and white pulses, the shimmer crawling up the torso toward the exposed chrome. Pants are wide-leg synth-leather in matte black with a single neon-orange stripe running from hip to ankle on the outer seam — the stripe is embedded with vibration-reactive thread that strobes during heavy beats. Footwear is chunky mag-sole boots with brushed steel toe caps, laces replaced with magnetic snap-clasps. A cropped open jacket in mesh-backed synth-leather sits over everything, left open to show the bodysuit beneath — the back panel carries a stenciled street tag in reflective ink. Neural port covers on the neck are swapped out for decorative chrome inserts shaped like radiating fins, catching club light with every head turn. Designed for someone whose chrome arms are the whole outfit.
functionality: Open-lattice shoulder and hip panels provide full range of motion for chrome augmented limbs with no fabric restriction. Reactive synthweave responds to sound frequencies without any power source — purely mechanical vibration response. Mag-sole boots provide stability on wet or grease-slicked club floors common in Circuit-tier venues.
what_it_says: Factory worker, transit op, or line tech who spent three months of discretionary income on one perfect night-out rig. The chrome arms aren't hidden — they're the whole presentation. This outfit says: I work with my body and my augments, and I'm not ashamed of either. The street tag on the back says which crew you run with after hours.
worn_by: augmented factory workers on nights off
transit operators with chrome limb replacements
rave-adjacent crew members with visible cyberware
story_hooks: A wearer's decorative chrome port covers accidentally interface with an experimental sound system at a Circuit club — the bass frequencies begin feeding directly into their neural port, and the experience is either transcendent or dangerous depending on their augment's firmware version.
The reflective street tag on the jacket back is recognized by a Tier 4 corporate security operative as the mark of a union-organizing cell — suddenly a night out becomes a surveillance situation.

Two people show up to the same club wearing near-identical Voltframe rigs — except one is the genuine street label and one is a corponation knockoff, and the original wearer intends to make the distinction very clear.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately incomplete look that makes augmented limbs the star — sleeveless compression core frames chrome, while oversized jacket drapes open like a stage curtain. Sharp, geometric aesthetic with deliberate negative space. Exudes circuit-club confidence and high-tier augmentation status.
physical_description.fit: Bodysuit: compression-tight on torso with strategic open lattice panels. Pants: wide-leg with tapered ankles. Jacket: cropped, oversized, worn fully open. Designed to showcase rather than conceal chrome augmentations.
physical_description.primary_material: Reactive synthweave bodysuit (gunmetal grey), matte black synth-leather pants, mesh-backed synth-leather jacket, brushed steel accents, vibration-reactive embedded thread
physical_description.texture: Smooth compression fabric with rippling surface tension. Lattice panels create geometric voids. Synth-leather has slight sheen. Reactive threads visible as thin metallic lines. Steel toe caps brushed matte.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey bodysuit, matte black pants with neon-orange embedded stripe, cropped jacket in dark synth-leather with reflective stencil art. Amber and white pulses animate the bodysuit during sound.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap-clasps on boots (replacing laces). Jacket left fully open. Bodysuit likely friction-fit compression with hidden closure or no fastening.
distinctive_features: Open-lattice panels at shoulders, hips, ribs — frames augmented limbs as sculpture
Bass-reactive synthweave that pulses amber/white with music
Neon-orange vibration-reactive stripe running hip to ankle
Cropped mesh-backed jacket with reflective stenciled street tag on back
Chrome decorative neural port covers shaped as radiating fins on neck
Magnetic snap-boot closures with brushed steel toe caps
Intentionally frameless design — the outfit is negative space
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2 circuit-club aesthetic — expensive augmentations on display, custom reactive fabrics, bespoke street-label construction. Signals wealth and corpo-adjacent cultural access.
physical_description.cultural_context: Circuit-club regular, augmentation enthusiast, someone at home in Tier 2 nightlife infrastructure. The outfit says: 'my chrome is my identity, and I dress to prove it.' Street-label pride mixed with high-grade augmentation flex.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to broken-in depending on wear frequency. Reactive elements remain functional. The stenciled jacket back may show intentional weathering for street credibility. Boots show scuff marks from dance floor use.
